note: Every place Nintendo's specification and the retail library disagree, and every place this package models something the specification does not settle. Each entry names what the document says, what the cartridges do, which one this package follows, and what evidence would close the question.
authority: hardware.json holds the ladder. Rung 1 is Nintendo's developer specification, rung 2 is a retail cartridge, rung 3 is nothing. The order is unusual here and deliberate: the specification is an instruction to a licensee rather than a description of silicon, so a genuine cartridge that disagrees with it is a fact about cartridges rather than an error.

divergences.topic: How the checksum is taken over an image whose length is not a power of two.

documentSays.claim: The remainder is added repeatedly until the total reaches a power of two.
documentSays.quote: If ROM size cannot be expressed evenly in 2nM bit, such as 10M or 20M bit, add the remainder until a total of 2nM bit is reached.
documentSays.source: SNES Development Manual Book 1, manual page 1-2-20, with worked examples for 12, 10, 20 and 24 megabit

thisPackageDid.claim: Summed every byte exactly once, whatever the length.
thisPackageDid.why: The manual carries two checksums with the same name and only one of them mirrors. The submission-sheet checksum on page 1-2-9 is a plain sum, and that page says so outright: "This method of calculation is different from the check sum on the ROM Registration Specification."

measured.note: Retail cartridges from the licensed regions whose own stored checksum and complement agree, so that there is something to be right about.

divergences.howItSurvived: Every property the census checked was internal: that the value and its complement are complements, that recomputing over the output gives back what was written, that nothing outside a header moved, that a second rewrite changes nothing. A rule wrong the same way every time passes all four. Nothing compared the computed value against the value the cartridge already carried, and that check has now been added as a fifth property named carried.
divergences.wouldReopenIt: A retail cartridge that is not a power of two, whose header is self-consistent, and whose stored checksum matches a plain sum and not the mirrored one, outside the SPC7110 images entry cartridges-that-still-disagree already names. Three of the 633 match a plain sum: both Tengai Makyou Zero images, which are two of those SPC7110 images, and Undake 30 - Same Game Daisakusen - Mario Version at 3 Mbit, where the two rules give the same value.

divergences.topic: Twelve retail images whose stored checksum is not the one the specification defines.

documentSays.claim: Every cartridge should carry the checksum the specification defines.

cartridgesDo.claim: Twelve of 2780 do not, and five of those twelve are a power of two, so mirroring is not what separates them.

groups.which: Campus Challenge '92, two PowerFest 94 titles, a MACS training cartridge marked as a bad dump
groups.reading: Three of these store a checksum of zero, which is not a checksum. These were never submitted through the process the specification governs.

groups.which: four Trials of Mana images from a Collection of Mana build, all storing the same value, and one Switch Online build of Pop'n TwinBee
groups.reading: Re-releases assembled decades later by a process that had no reason to honour a submission requirement.

groups.which: both Tengai Makyou Zero images at 40 Mbit, chipset F9H, and Momotarou Dentetsu Happy at 24 Mbit, chipset F5H, all three carrying maker code 18
groups.reading: Narrowed, not explained. Each stored value is reproduced from the image bytes alone, with the four checksum bytes neutral and no address mapping applied: both Tengai Makyou Zero images carry the plain sum of every byte counted once, and Momotarou Dentetsu Happy carries twice that plain sum. A sum over the first megabyte alone, the program ROM an SPC7110 board splits off from its data ROM, matches none of the three and does not match Super Power League 4, the fourth SPC7110 image, either. No rule this package could adopt covers them: the 20 other retail images carrying maker code 18 that are not a power of two follow the specified mirrored sum, Daikaijuu Monogatari II among them at the same 40 Mbit as Tengai Makyou Zero, so the departure belongs to these SPC7110 titles rather than to the publisher's sizes.

divergences.consequence: This package computes the specified checksum for these images, which is not the one they carry. Rewriting one of them therefore changes its checksum to the specified value.
wouldSettleIt: For the SPC7110 group, a Nintendo or licensee document saying how the header checksum is taken on an SPC7110 board. The arithmetic is measured; what is missing is why the tool that mastered these titles summed the file once, or twice, instead of mirroring it. No further cartridge can settle it, because all four retail SPC7110 images are in the census.
For the competition, prototype and re-release groups, nothing outside reach would change the reading: they were never submitted through the process the specification governs.
divergences.why: Named rather than folded into a pass rate. Twelve is small and three of them are unexplained, and a summary that reported only the agreement figure would hide that.

measured.subjects: The 2,780 retail images from the licensed regions with a self-consistent header, the population the carried observation reports, which reproduced its figures: 2,768 agree with the specified sum, and of the 633 that are not a power of two, 626 agree with the mirrored sum and 3 with a plain one.
measured.spc7110: Every retail image declaring chipset F5H or F9H: 4 images, 3 titles. Specified mirrored sum matches 1, Super Power League 4 at 16 Mbit, where every candidate rule agrees. Program ROM only, the first 0x100000 bytes, matches 0 of 4. Plain sum matches both Tengai Makyou Zero images. Twice the plain sum matches Momotarou Dentetsu Happy, and it was the only hit among 4,096 weightings of 0 to 3 applied to each of its six 512 KB blocks, against about 0.06 hits expected by chance.
measured.control: The 20 other non-power-of-two retail images with maker code 18, the publisher of all three, every one agreeing with the specified mirrored sum and none with a plain sum except Undake 30, where the two coincide.

divergences.topic: That an image contains several byte-identical copies of its header.

documentSays.claim: Nothing. The specification gives one registration area per map mode and never mentions copies.

cartridgesDo.claim: Carry up to thirty two identical copies, because the same bank is visible at several addresses.

divergences.consequence: Every mirror is rewritten and every mirror's neutral bytes are set before the sum. A tool that updates one copy produces an image that works in whichever reader it was tested against.
wouldSettleIt: Nothing. The specification and the cartridges do not disagree: a mirror is what the address decoding produces from one registration area, so both describe the same image. It is recorded because a tool that rewrote one copy would produce an image that works in whichever reader it was tested against, and that is worth a reader knowing.

divergences.topic: Two coprocessor codes whose upper nibble the specification does not list.

documentSays.claim: Six upper nibbles: 0 for DSP, 1 for Super FX, 2 for OBC1, 3 for SA-1, E for Other and F for Custom Chip.
documentSays.quote: Cartridge Type (FFD6H). Indicate the game pak (cartridge) configuration. Use one of the tables below, depending upon whether or not a co-processor is used.
documentSays.source: SNES Development Manual Book 1, manual page 1-2-18

cartridgesDo.claim: Retail cartridges carry 43H and 45H for the S-DD1 and 55H for the S-RTC, whose upper nibbles are 4 and 5. Neither appears in the table.
cartridgesDo.examples: Star Ocean and Street Fighter Alpha 2 carry the S-DD1 codes; Daikaijuu Monogatari II carries the S-RTC code.

divergences.consequence: This package names those three codes and treats them as coprocessor declarations, which is what a rewrite has to do to clear them. Nothing about them rests on a Nintendo document.
divergences.why: The revision of the specification read here predates those parts. Nintendo either extended the table in a later revision nobody has published, or assigned the codes without doing so. Either way the cartridges are the fact and the table is incomplete rather than contradicted.
wouldSettleIt: A later revision of the development manual with a longer table.
A Nintendo licensee bulletin assigning the codes.

divergences.topic: How to declare a size the manual's table does not list.

documentSays.claim: A five row table covering 3 to 64 megabit, and nothing below or above it.
documentSays.quote: ROM Size (FFD7H). The program ROM size is stored at this address. Select the appropriate code from the table below.
documentSays.source: SNES Development Manual Book 1, manual page 1-2-19

divergences.consequence: This package computes the base two logarithm of the size in kilobytes, rounded up, which reproduces every row printed and also answers for sizes the table does not cover.
divergences.why: A table with five rows cannot be the whole rule, because cartridges smaller than 3 megabit exist and carry a size byte. Extending by the pattern the printed rows follow is a smaller invention than picking a nearest row.
wouldSettleIt: A Nintendo document giving the rule as a formula, or a table with more rows.

divergences.topic: The 512 byte block some dumps carry in front of the image.

documentSays.claim: Nothing. It is a product of hardware Nintendo did not sell.

divergences.consequence: The stub is stripped before anything else happens, so every offset in this file is an offset into the image the console would see.
divergences.wouldReopenIt: Nothing. There is no Nintendo document to reconcile with, and there never will be.
